slot.subtopic: Perpendicular distance from point to line
slot.brief: 3D line in vector/cartesian form and an external point; find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular and the shortest distance from the point to the line.

stem: The line $(x,y,z)=(1,0,1)+t(1,2,2)$ and the point $P(5,3,5)$ are given. Find the foot of the perpendicular from $P$ to the line and the shortest distance, respectively.

verdicts.working: For direction vector v=(1,2,2) and P−a=(4,3,4), t=((P−a)·v)/(v·v)=18/9=2. Thus the foot is (3,4,5), and the distance is √((2)^2+(-1)^2)=√5.

working:
$\mathbf v=(1,2,2),\quad P-A=(4,3,4)$; $t=\dfrac{(P-A)\cdot\mathbf v}{|\mathbf v|^2}=\dfrac{18}{9}=2$; $N=A+2\mathbf v=(3,4,5)$; $|P-N|=|(2,-1,0)|=\sqrt5$.

Independent check: For direction vector v=(1,2,2) and P−a=(4,3,4), t=((P−a)·v)/(v·v)=18/9=2. Thus the foot is (3,4,5), and the distance is √((2)^2+(-1)^2)=√5.
solution:
For line point $A=(1,0,1)$ and direction $v=(1,2,2)$, the perpendicular foot is $N=A+tv$, where $t=\dfrac{(P-A)\cdotv}{|v|^2}=\dfrac{18}{9}=2$.
Thus $N=(1,0,1)+2(1,2,2)=(3,4,5)$, and $PN=\sqrt{(5-3)^2+(3-4)^2+(5-5)^2}=\sqrt5$.
